mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates accommodative monetary policy, which lowers discount rates and boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS remains below 0.5% for 3 consecutive months and S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 7.5% signals a weak labor market and potential economic contraction, which typically results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE exceeds 7.5%, the S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of the cases over the next 5 days.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent weakness in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based slowdown in consumer demand, which negatively impacts corporate earnings and leads to S&P 500 underperformance over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When both HOUST and RSAFS are below their 30th percentile, the S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the cases.

mechanism_narrative: A monetary tightening cycle, defined by a sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS), leads to higher discount rates and reduced liquidity, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: During periods when FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25 percentage points over 3 months, the S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Robust job growth (PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market and healthy economic expansion, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS growth is above 0.5% month-over-month, the S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of the cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 450.0 thousand units signals weakness in the housing sector, which is a key driver of consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST falls below 450.0, the S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of the cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous weakness in industrial production (INDPRO) and GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates a contraction in the real economy, which reduces corporate profitability and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When both INDPRO and GDPC1 are below their 40th percentile, the S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, characterized by low unemployment (UNRATE) and high industrial production (INDPRO), the economy faces supply-side constraints that lead to inflationary pressures and subsequent monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE < 5.5% and INDPRO > 105, the S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.
